clue.text: Postage to be delivered by secret service

indicators.note: the letters are to be delivered like a parcel, freed from their order and set down afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A parcel's postage is being carried by an intelligence agency's couriers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police of Nazi Germany, a notorious example of a security force.

clue.text: Lift victorious day up in lift

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up reads the letters from bottom to top
one piece sits inside the other, enclosed by its letters

blocks.note: VE Day celebrated victory in Europe in 1945
to lift someone's spirits is to elate them

explanation.surface: An instruction to raise the mood on a day of triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: The word lift appears twice: once as the definition, once meaning to cheer up.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate something is to raise it higher, a plain synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Soundly munched on a house

indicators.note: soundly means as heard when spoken, not as written on the page

blocks.note: munched on a is chewed a, said quickly in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Someone noisily gnawing away at a building.
explanation.walkthrough: Say chewed a quickly and it gives the name of the royal dynasty. House here means a ruling family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were a royal house of England, the dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Ingredient of soup, other broth's flavouring

indicators.note: an ingredient is part of a mixture, so the letters form part of the following words

blocks.note: spans the end of soup, all of other and the start of broth

explanation.surface: A recipe note about what gives a second broth its taste.
explanation.definitionFit: A potherb is a herb grown for cooking, used to season soups and stews.

clue.text: Grain, or 28

blocks.note: first meaning: corn scattered for poultry
second meaning: peanuts, a trivially small sum of money

explanation.walkthrough: 28 points to the answer at 28-across, read in its slang sense of a paltry amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn thrown to hens is literal poultry food, and figuratively the phrase means a negligible sum, as peanuts does.

clue.text: Listed at last?

blocks.note: first meaning: a ship that has listed has leaned over to one side
second meaning: a shoe on the cobbler's last gets a heel fitted

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as finally being put on a list; a last is a foot-shaped block on which shoes are made and mended.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel heels when it tilts in the water, and a shoe is heeled when the cobbler fits its back part.

clue.text: Reportedly, one over the eight wants curry on top of a male 5

definitions.note: describes the crest on a cockerel's head

indicators.note: reportedly means by word of mouth, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: the cox steers and commands a rowing eight
to curry a horse is to groom it, as with a currycomb

explanation.surface: A drunk, one over the eight, craves a curry before tackling a chicken dish.
explanation.walkthrough: One over the eight normally means tipsy; here it is the person in charge of eight rowers. 5 refers to the answer at 5-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockscomb is the fleshy red crest growing on the head of a rooster.

clue.text: Award appended to noble appendage

indicators.note: appended to means added after, so the award follows the noble in the grid

blocks.note: an earl is a British peer
the Order of the British Empire, an honour

explanation.surface: An honour tacked on to a peer's title.
explanation.definitionFit: The lobe is the soft hanging part of the outer ear, a small body appendage.

clue.text: Backing arranged, having acted as solicitor

blocks.note: being pro something is backing it
things arranged have been positioned

explanation.surface: A lawyer who set up financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitor suggests a lawyer; here it is one who solicits, making an improper offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To proposition someone is to solicit them, so having done so is having acted as one who solicits.

clue.text: See 5
Welshman with French horn breaks into the old-fashioned number

indicators.note: a burglar breaking into a house ends up inside it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: a common Welsh name
cor is French for horn
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Welsh player with his horn bursting into a vintage song.
explanation.walkthrough: Number looks like a song; it is a quantity, sixty.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, so three of them make sixty, a biblical, archaic way of counting.

clue.text: Author wants hedge trimmed

indicators.note: a trimmed hedge has its end cut off, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: a hedge is a barrier between fields

explanation.surface: A writer asking for the garden hedge to be cut.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish novelist and playwright who created Peter Pan.

clue.text: In which reporters harass and fight?

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a place, standing for the noun

blocks.note: to press someone is to harass them
boxing is fighting

explanation.surface: Journalists in their enclosure pestering and brawling.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description of the place too: reporters both harass and scrap there.
explanation.definitionFit: The press box is the stand reserved for journalists at a sports ground.

clue.text: Plain cream is all you can give

blocks.note: a plain is flat, level ground
the cream of something is its best part

explanation.surface: Plain cream is all a dairy has to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing your level best means making the greatest possible effort, giving all you have.

clue.text: Removing hair, arrange into a pile

indicators.note: to arrange is to put in a fresh order, so the following letters get reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Instructions for sweeping up shorn locks into a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Epilation is depilation by the roots, the technical term for getting rid of body hair.

clue.text: "The Arabian Nights" number takes time for a 29

blocks.note: the tales are the Thousand and One Nights: M is a thousand in Roman numerals, plus one
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A storyteller's tale gets timed for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist artist famous for his water lilies.

clue.text: Sack the band

blocks.note: first meaning: to plunder, despoil
second meaning: a long narrow piece of material

explanation.surface: Fire the whole group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Sack and band suggest firing a pop group; this is also the theme word, a comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip a town is to plunder it bare, and a strip is a narrow length like a band of cloth.

clue.text: Fall in support for student

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, enclosed

blocks.note: a golf tee supports the ball
rain is what falls from the sky

explanation.surface: Someone collapsing into a prop meant for a learner.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee is someone learning a job, much as a student is learning.

clue.text: Doing 14 for our 17?

blocks.note: surface reading: trying as hard as possible for the newspaper's comic strip
setter's reading: our strip is the Guardian's, so the answer is the cartoonist who draws it

explanation.walkthrough: 14 and 17 point to the answers LEVEL BEST and STRIP. Steve Bell drew the long-running If... strip in the Guardian, where this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoonist working for the paper that printed the puzzle produced its strip, hopefully trying his hardest.

clue.text: Lynn and Dicky on stage outdoors

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so the letters are unsound and get rearranged

blocks.note: Dame Vera Lynn, the wartime singer
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Two performers, Lynn and Dicky, appearing in an open-air show.
explanation.walkthrough: Dicky looks like a second performer's name; it is the anagram signal. Vera Lynn was the Forces' Sweetheart of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed platform along the outside of a house, a raised outdoor floor.

clue.text: Insects delightful? Not one - that's right!

indicators.note: not one means without the numeral one, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: lice are small parasitic insects
nice means pleasant or delightful

explanation.surface: Someone protesting that bugs are lovely, then conceding none are.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the Roman numeral for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is a permission or entitlement, as when one has the right to do something.

clue.text: Dress with which I try to get into the groove

indicators.note: getting into something means ending up inside it, enclosed

blocks.note: a rut is a groove worn in the ground
I plus GO, a try or attempt

explanation.surface: An outfit worn for getting into the groove on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rig-out is an informal British word for an outfit or set of clothes.

clue.text: Sea battle requires most of warships and one in Florentine river

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is lost
in places the single letter inside the river's name

blocks.note: a navy is a fleet of warships
the Arno flows through Florence
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A naval engagement needs most of the fleet plus a ship on an Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: Navarino, in 1827, was a naval battle in which allied fleets destroyed the Ottoman–Egyptian navy.

clue.text: Country doctor leaves, admitting love of French style

indicators.note: leaves means goes away from, so the doctor departs from the country's name
admitting means letting in, so the remaining letters take something inside

blocks.note: a North African country
MO is a medical officer
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A rural GP quits, confessing a fondness for Gallic design.
explanation.walkthrough: Country doctor looks like one phrase for a rural GP; it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century decorative manner that originated in France under Louis XV.

clue.text: Acadian preparation of 5, taking about a month

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, as in a style of chicken dish

blocks.note: ca is short for circa, about
Jun is the abbreviation for June

explanation.surface: A Louisiana chicken recipe that takes weeks to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 refers to the answer at 5-across, chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajuns are Louisianans of Acadian descent, and their spicy cooking style gives Cajun chicken.

clue.text: On the mountains, negotiating summit with oxygen, at the world's extremities

indicators.note: to negotiate a pass is to get through it, so the mountain word wraps around what comes through

blocks.note: Andean means of the Andes
a tip is the top
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: Climbers in the Andes tackling a peak with bottled oxygen, far from home.
explanation.definitionFit: The antipodes are places diametrically opposite on the globe, typically Australia and New Zealand seen from Britain.

clue.text: 17 for each 17?

blocks.note: surface reading: strip for each strip, an odd repetition
setter's reading: in every episode of her comic strip the heroine undressed

explanation.walkthrough: 17 is the answer STRIP. Jane was a Daily Mirror comic strip from 1932 whose heroine kept losing her clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon heroine was famous for undressing in each instalment of the newspaper strip named after her.

clue.text: 17, though not much to show for it!

definitions.text: not much to show for it

blocks.note: first meaning: Charles Schulz's comic strip, 17 being STRIP

blocks.clueFragment: not much to show for it
blocks.note: second meaning: a paltry reward, slang for very little money

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation suggests a strip-cartoonist's meagre pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts is the Snoopy and Charlie Brown cartoon, and peanuts is slang for a trivial payment.

clue.text: Craftsman needed to secure craft?

blocks.note: first meaning: a decorator or artist who applies colour
second meaning: a rope at a boat's bow for tying it up

explanation.walkthrough: Craft shifts from skill to boat between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is a skilled tradesman with brushes, and also the mooring line used to tie a small boat.
